newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE eyeing Eastern Europe but liquidity lacks.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE eyeing Eastern Europe but liquidity lacks.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) is looking at the scope for Eastern European derivatives but liquidity is a problem and any plans would be a long way off, LIFFE's chief executive said.
"There's no question but that we have been looking at Eastern European and other European possibilities," LIFFE chief executive Daniel Hodson said in an interview with Reuters.
"But it's very important to do these things with the correct timing and there may not be a sufficiently liquid market demand for a future of many of these products yet," Hodson said.

Hodson said LIFFE routinely conducted formal reviews of money markets and bonds both inside and outside the European timezone. The exchange looked at market depth and quality to determine potential for a new derivative product.
"In so many of these cases we aren't there yet," he said, but he added, "There is a degree of progress."
Hodson said any plans in this area would be very long term as most European exchanges are devoting their energines to preparing for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
The new euro currency under EMU is due to start on January 1, 1999.
